[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is nuclear RNA production and maturation: an RNA polymerase I subunit supports ribosomal RNA transcription, a small-subunit processome component participates in pre-rRNA processing toward ribosome assembly, a general transcription factor subunit assists RNA polymerase II promoter opening, a spliceosome-associated crooked-neck-like factor acts in pre-mRNA splicing, and a core exosome subunit provides 3' to 5' exoribonuclease-mediated RNA trimming and surveillance; loss of that exosome subunit causes cerebellar hypoplasia with spinal motor neuron degeneration. [untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.
